sheets.character_en: The March Hare, a male animal: a photoreal adult wild brown hare, lanky, long-legged and springy, about 50 cm tall sitting up (ears add about 10 cm), real hare anatomy throughout. In all three full-body views he sits up on his haunches. Coarse, unkempt fur sticking up in tufts with wisps of straw caught in it: tawny russet-brown flecked with black on the back, sandy flanks, a white belly and chin, a black-topped white tail. A long hare head with very long black-tipped ears that swivel independently; large, round, bulging amber-gold eyes set high on the sides of the head, staring; dark nose leather, a twitching nose, a long split upper lip, front incisors showing. Gloomy, staring look carried by ears and eyes only; no human expression.
sheets.prompt_final: Four-panel creature reference sheet following the reference layout: three full-body views of the animal (front / side / back) left to right, and one large head close-up filling the right column; the exact same animal, markings and proportions in every panel; plain background. The sheet looks like four production photographs mounted side by side on one board: the image is divided by three thin vertical gaps into three narrow full-height panels on the left and one wide panel on the right; each panel is its own small photograph and the animal is scaled to fit completely inside each narrow panel. Panel 1: full-body front view, facing the camera. Panel 2: full-body side profile view facing right. Panel 3: full-body back view. Panel 4 (right column): large close-up of the head and chest, facing the camera or a slight three-quarter turn, eyes, nose and whiskers sharp. Macro studio photography at the animal's own eye level: in each full-body view the whole animal, including the ears, feet and the full tail, sits inside the panel with clear space around it, on a small patch of floor with a soft contact shadow. Plain seamless warm light-grey studio backdrop in every panel, soft even light, no scenery, no props other than those named below. Identity lock: one and the same individual animal in all four panels, with identical fur or scale pattern, markings, eye colour and build; exactly one animal per panel; no duplicated or extra animals. Character: The March Hare, a male animal: a photoreal adult wild brown hare, lanky, long-legged and springy, about 50 cm tall sitting up (ears add about 10 cm), real hare anatomy throughout. In all three full-body views he sits up on his haunches. Coarse, unkempt fur sticking up in tufts with wisps of straw caught in it: tawny russet-brown flecked with black on the back, sandy flanks, a white belly and chin, a black-topped white tail. A long hare head with very long black-tipped ears that swivel independently; large, round, bulging amber-gold eyes set high on the sides of the head, staring; dark nose leather, a twitching nose, a long split upper lip, front incisors showing. Gloomy, staring look carried by ears and eyes only; no human expression. Costume: unclothed and unadorned: the bare natural hare, wearing nothing. Style: Photorealistic live-action fantasy film rooted in England in 1862, shot on 35mm film with anamorphic lenses, 16:9 widescreen. Real sets, real locations and real costumed actors in 1862 dress. Wonderland spaces are real built sets and set extensions in an Alphonse Mucha-inspired Art Nouveau design: flowing organic lines, floral and vine ornament, circular halo roundels, mosaic and stained glass, aged pastel-and-gold surfaces with patina and moss; the waking 1862 meadow stays plain period realism. Talking animals and fantastical creatures are photoreal CGI animals with naturalistic anatomy, real fur, feathers, skin and scales, lit by the same light and grounded with real contact shadows. Natural and practical light: sunlight, candlelight and oil lamps, soft haze with volumetric light shafts and soft colour through stained glass. Restrained palette of verdigris teal, slate grey, dusty rose, soft sage and lilac pastels and tarnished-gold accents, warmed by amber sun and candle glow. Fine film grain, gentle halation, soft depth of field, grounded and quietly melancholy. Layout recap (highest priority): four separate photographic panels side by side on one sheet: front, side profile, back, head close-up; plain studio backdrop; never one single full-bleed picture; a real photographed animal, not a cartoon.
